scenario: adversarial review of the upstream module-set / tag-pin / dependency-metadata changes before the rc.3 release
method: manual red-team review with executable attack tests and real-jar/real-network verification; an independent subagent audit was attempted but the provider quota was exhausted, so the audit was performed in-session

propositions.claim: branch target_commitish plus tag resolution does not weaken the release trust chain
attacks: tag chain that does not resolve to one full commit SHA -> rejected (releaseChannelWithoutMatchingCiOrResolvableTagIsRejected)
successful CI missing on the resolved commit -> rejected (same test)
offline pending plan with tampered commit -> rejected by verifyRun head_sha binding (branchTargetPlanAppliesOfflineAndRejectsTamperedCommit)
release changed during download -> existing fingerprint re-check
older or reused CI sequence -> existing per-scope high-water and fingerprint checks
propositions.residual: branch-target plans cannot re-resolve the tag offline; the binding is verified at staging and the downloaded bytes remain digest-verified. A tag moved between resolution and download leaves the recorded commit possibly different from the actual build commit, the same trust class as SHA-target releases whose recorded target is fixed at creation.

propositions.claim: dynamic module acceptance cannot mix builds, silently skip selections, or break ownership/recovery
attacks: release missing core or vanilla -> rejected (releaseMissingRequiredModuleMixingVersionsOrDuplicatingAssetsIsRejected)
mixed module versions in one release -> rejected (same test)
selected retired module -> explicit rejection before any download (retiredSelectedModuleIsRejectedWithGuidanceAndNoPending, live probe step 4)
unknown upstream folkways asset ignored while unknown installed folkways-named JAR stays protected (unknownUpstreamAssetsAreIgnoredButUnknownInstalledFolkwaysJarsStayProtected)
deselected owned integrations removed at apply while prerequisites retained (deselectingRetiredIntegrationsRemovesOwnedJarsOnTheNextModernInstall)
explicit takeover of assistant with bundled jpimini (modernAssistantWithBundledJpiminiCanBeTakenOverExplicitly)
propositions.note: ownership of newly installed files begins at apply, not at staging; the takeover test initially asserted the wrong stage and was corrected

propositions.claim: defaulting an omitted dependency type to required neither admits rejected metadata nor misclassifies optional dependencies
evidence: NeoForge official documentation states type defaults to required (docs.neoforged.net Mod Files, Dependency Configurations)
typeless dependency enforced as required; unknown type still rejected (omittedDependencyTypeDefaultsToRequiredLikeNeoForge)
real Sable 2.0.6 with bundled Veil 4.3.2 / sablecompanion 1.6.0 parsed and installed through the production path (live probe step 2)
propositions.residual: versionRange remains mandatory for required dependencies although NeoForge allows an empty range meaning any version; this is stricter and fail-closed, and may reject a future jar that omits versionRange

propositions.claim: the sable pin matches the official Modrinth version and the real jar
evidence: project T9PomCSv / version fg9dTRz9 / file sable-neoforge-1.21.1-2.0.6.jar / size 12986135 / sha512 76d293ce... verified against api.modrinth.com and the downloaded bytes
jar mod identity {sable: 2.0.6} matches the pin; airline exact pin [2.0.6] satisfied
live install downloaded and hash-verified through the production pin path

propositions.claim: the dormant signed manifest channel has no regression
evidence: SIGNED_MODULES keeps the five-module manifest contract; Config rejects new modules when manifestUrl is set (moduleVocabularyFollowsChannel)
full signed-manifest test suite passes unchanged

propositions.claim: tests exercise failure and recovery paths rather than restating the implementation
evidence: added: missing required module, mixed versions, duplicate asset, offline branch-target apply with tamper, retired selection, typeless/unknown dependency type, channel module vocabulary, assistant takeover
187 core tests, 185 pass, 2 platform-specific skips; 26 companion tests pass; 95 Python publisher tests pass

propositions.claim: the dynamic module set does not break the sync state machine or readback
evidence: modern four-module layout accepted; missing core/vanilla rejected; mixed-layout sources synced with per-source asset counts; unknown modules not synced (test_sync_openlist.py)
asset regex built from the sorted known set and used with fullmatch; single-version check retained

propositions.claim: message mapping, localization, layout and resource limits remain bounded
evidence: retired-module mapping regex bounded to lowercase module lists; both locale files carry the new keys
config screen keeps five rows within 320x240; client smoke source compiles and asserts bounds
CI Windows full pass; Ubuntu failed once on a Maven Central HTTP 429 while resolving the buildscript classpath (infrastructure), retried by the next push

conclusion: pass; release may proceed after both-platform CI is green
